_comment: Baked by scripts/bake_updates.py from hebrish.app/changelog; do not edit by hand. Shown offline in the apps' What's new (Android Updates screen, desktop About tab).

entries.title: Clearer controls in the voice keyboard
entries.summary: The Hebrish voice keyboard has one row of round, colour-coded buttons: Discard (red), Retake (amber), the mic in the middle, Pause (gold while paused) and Insert last.

entries.title: Enter waits for your last words, fewer repeated words, and Voice Typing
entries.summary: In the Hebrish voice keyboard, if you tap Enter after you stop and before the last words are in, the Enter now waits for them (up to 4 seconds), then sends.

entries.title: Voice Typing, late words kept out of your next message, fewer repeated words
entries.summary: If you press Enter after you stop and before the last words are in, those words no longer land in whatever you type next, such as the next prompt in a chat box.

entries.title: No more half-words where a long dictation is split
entries.summary: Longer dictations are decoded in pieces cut at your pauses. The first word after a pause sometimes lost its start ("ividual" for "individual", "chnically" for "technically"); it now comes out whole, on Android and on the desktop.

entries.title: Switch your remote's buttons off without losing them, and save sets of them
entries.summary: Settings, Sound, microphone and buttons has a new Use bound buttons switch. Turn it off and Hebrish takes no keys, so the same Bluetooth remote works in other apps; your bindings are kept for when you turn it back on.

entries.title: Models in plain words, a What's new list, and the floating mic types instead of pasting
entries.summary: Each model now says what it's built on, for example "Base model: Parakeet 0.6B v2 by NVIDIA"; the technical detail is under Technical details.

entries.title: Sabich v2.1: more recordings, and no more <unk>
entries.summary: Sabich v2.1 replaces v2.0 as the recommended model in the apps. It is a Sabich-only update to Release v2; Shakshuka, Jachnun and Meorav are unchanged.

entries.title: Your microphones in your order, and no more lost words
entries.summary: Settings has a Microphones list: every mic Hebrish has seen on this computer, with a name you give it and a type (built-in, headset, wireless headset, shotgun, lav, dynamic and more).

entries.title: Paragraphs in Transcription Mode, your choice of how
entries.summary: Transcription Mode, in both apps, has a Paragraphs setting: None (one block of text), Time-based (a new paragraph about every 30 seconds, as before) or Paragraph model.

entries.title: Transcription Mode, the next take any time, and no more "um"
entries.summary: Transcription Mode, in both apps: record a long take, then transcribe it.

entries.title: Hebrish 1.0: the floating mic gets out of the way, desktop output you can combine, and Paste last
entries.summary: Both apps are now version 1.000. From here, versions count 1.001, 1.002, and so on, on Android and desktop alike.

entries.title: A cleaner look, and the floating mic keeps your line breaks
entries.summary: The app's screens now use the Hebrish look from this site: the warm paper background, the green accent, the Hebrish logo (it was showing as a plain green square), headings in the Hebrish typeface and grouped settings on the home screen.

entries.title: A personal dictionary: your words, written your way
entries.summary: Add the words you want written a certain way: names, brands, Hebrew words in the spelling you use. After each take, Hebrish replaces what the model wrote with your spelling.

entries.title: Android: fewer capitals and full stops in the middle of sentences
entries.summary: Long takes are transcribed in pieces at your pauses, and each piece used to be treated as a sentence of its own, so a pause mid-sentence could leave "word. Capital".

entries.title: Desktop: fewer capitals and full stops in the middle of sentences
entries.summary: With insert as you go, stopping to think in the middle of a sentence no longer ends it. Each piece of text is now transcribed together with the end of the piece before it, so the model hears that the sentence carries on and writes it the way it would mid-sentence.

entries.title: Android: transcription history, exported as CSV
entries.summary: Every take is now kept on your phone: the text, its length, the model, and how long it took to transcribe. Under Dictation, Export CSV saves it through the file picker, so you can put it straight into Google Drive.

entries.title: Android: minimise the floating mic with a double-tap
entries.summary: When the floating mic is in the way of what you are writing, double-tap it and it shrinks to a small dot in the same place.

entries.title: Android: the floating mic keeps your line breaks
entries.summary: With the floating mic, a line break typed before dictating (to start a new paragraph, say) was deleted when the text arrived, and a space put in its place.

entries.title: Terms of use 1.2: every model listed
entries.summary: The licence table now lists every model line: Jachnun, Sabich and its variants on other bases, Shakshuka, Meorav and the Whisper fine-tunes, each with the licence it was released under.

entries.title: Desktop: change how dictation is inserted from the tray
entries.summary: The tray menu has an Output submenu: paste at the cursor, clipboard only, or the app's own text box, and the paste shortcut (Ctrl+V, or Ctrl+Shift+V for terminals).
